terms.context: US labor market: monthly job gains needed to hold the unemployment rate steady

clip_research.source_claim: The U.S. economy needs to add only about 40,000 jobs a month to keep the unemployment rate steady, and the latest Fed rate hike was not justified.
clip_research.public_baseline: Federal Reserve Bank research (St. Louis Fed, Dallas Fed, Federal Reserve notes) treats breakeven employment growth as a moving estimate that depends on labor force growth, immigration, and participation; recent 2026 estimates show the range widening and the breakeven rate declining as unauthorized immigration outflows reduce labor force growth.
clip_research.surprise_gap: The speaker's 40,000/month figure is presented as a firm break-even rate, while public Fed research frames breakeven employment as an uncertain, widening range rather than a single stable number.

evidence.fact: Speaker says the U.S. job market must add 40,000 jobs a month to hold the unemployment rate steady, citing demographic change and lower net immigration.
Speaker says the last three months averaged 51,000 jobs and 2026 has run about 65,000 a month, with the unemployment rate moving only from 4.14 to 4.17.

winning_patterns: 机构/人物权威 + 具体数字/资产 + 强问题，例如 高盛王逸：4-5万亿城市更新会拖住楼市吗
大机构/名人 + 被逼/陷阱/真相/转向 等张力词，例如 野村辜朝明：日本央行被逼到墙角
具体数据 + 政策动作疑问，例如 6月PMI释放积极信号，政府会加码吗
